prompt: Review this anchor as its assigned subagent. Enumerate ALL requirements, qualifications, edge cases and scenarios. Inspect all supplied implementation and test fragments and trace each aspect to implementation behavior and actual test assertions or justified TODO/N/A evidence. Passing tests and associations alone are insufficient. Follow helpers and capture every additional source dependency with cargo meta review read ANCHOR PATH [selector] before completing the report. Explain prerequisites for justified TODO tests; do not claim deferred behavior is implemented. Distinguish source inspection from commands actually executed. Write a JSON report containing reviewer, report, and requested_edits. Leave requested_edits empty only when every aspect is accounted for and no edits are needed. Otherwise list concrete changes, including missing tests or justified TODO tests with prerequisite comments. Run cargo meta review record ANCHOR REPORT_FILE to finish. After edits or stale-input rejection, run cargo meta review start ANCHOR and review the fresh inputs. The gate fails until a current report with no requested edits is recorded. Dependency capture is agent-declared.
coordinator_instructions:
Follow sage-review-checklist for only the assigned anchor. Begin fresh review using cargo meta review start ANCHOR --instructions /tmp/ci-anchor-review-instructions.txt. Inspect current claim, implementation, complete tests, and capture dependencies through review read. Independently assess current evidence; do not transplant old approvals. Preserve justified TODO/N/A entries honestly. Record a complete claim-specific report. Coordinate all source edits with root BEFORE editing, to avoid invalidating concurrent reviews. Prefer reporting concrete necessary changes for root to batch; do not add unrelated evidence. You own only your assigned validation directory and unique /tmp report. Distinguish source inspection from tests executed. Do not commit.
Root centrally runs relevant suites. Do not repeat full suites for a source-only review unless investigating a specific concern. Report source assessment honestly without claiming execution. This does not waive regression reproduction for suspected bugs.

Keyed lowering boundary over owned Tcx facts. The concrete rustc service lives in sage-rustc-bridge; sage-ir does not depend on that implementation.

**External metadata supplies owned facts, never Sage decisions.** The provider may state facts authored by a reachable dependency or the compiler, but it cannot resolve local syntax, select a Sage candidate, prove a Sage goal, normalize an alias, or type-check a Sage body. This is the typed metadata boundary established by [External providers supply facts, not Sage semantic answers](../../../rfds/architectural-foundations/README.md#external-providers-supply-facts-not-sage-semantic-answers).

**Missing metadata remains explicit incompleteness.** A missing, unsupported, or conservatively incomplete external fact is never replaced by an inferred default, a successful interface, or exhaustive logical failure. This is the metadata consequence of [Incompleteness is an explicit terminal outcome](../../../rfds/architectural-foundations/README.md#incompleteness-is-an-explicit-terminal-outcome).

**External demand is decomposed by semantic product.** Identity enumeration, signatures, impl headers, and individual associated values are separate tracked products. Consumers enumerate identities before requesting selected details, and no external function body is available to checking. This is the metadata consequence of [Cross-item dependencies stop at semantic interfaces](../../../rfds/architectural-foundations/README.md#cross-item-dependencies-stop-at-semantic-interfaces).

**Raw and lowered metadata share the same narrow reuse key.** Each lowered semantic fact observes only its corresponding owned provider fact. Repeating an unchanged request reuses the lowered value without another raw request, and changing an unrelated provider fact does not invalidate it.

## External providers supply facts, not Sage semantic answers
Rustc-backed providers may authoritatively expose facts owned by reachable
dependency crates and the compilation environment: definition identity,
ownership, signatures, predicates, associated items and values, impl headers,
and other exported metadata. Sage lowers those facts into its own symbol,
type, stash, and query representations at narrow keyed boundaries.
The provider does not resolve Sage-local source, select a method or impl for a
Sage body, prove a Sage trait goal, normalize an alias on Sage's behalf, or
produce Sage's checked body. Those operations remain in Sage even when their
inputs include authoritative external facts. Likewise, the rustc side of the
oracle is an independent comparison producer, not a hidden semantic service
This boundary makes external metadata reusable without masking gaps in Sage's
semantics or creating accidental whole-crate dependencies. Its local contract
